questions.question: Which of the following road signs warn that you are approaching an intersection where you have the right of way?

options.text: Sign A
Sign B
Sign C
Sign D

questions.explanation: On a crossroad warning sign the thicker line shows the road that has priority; the correct sign has the thicker line in your direction of travel. Still approach with caution and be ready to stop if cross traffic does not yield.

questions.question: A motor car is carrying goods on its roof rack. What is the maximum height that the load may extend above the highest point of the roof?

options.text: One-third of the height of the motor car measured from ground level
One-half of the height of the motor car measured from ground level
1 metre above the roof
There is no restriction provided the load is secured

questions.explanation: Goods on the roof of a motor car may not extend above the highest point of the roof by more than half the height of the car measured from ground level.

questions.question: A driver sees a drift warning sign and an "Occasional Flooding supplementary plate. The road appears dry and several vehicles have recently crossed the area. Which assumption would be the LEAST safe?

options.text: Water levels can change quickly after rainfall elsewhere in the area
The warning remains relevant even when the road is dry
Conditions should still be assessed before crossing
The absence of visible water means the flooding hazard no longer exists

questions.explanation: A drift with an 'Occasional Flooding' plate warns that flooding can occur intermittently; a dry surface now does not remove the risk, so D is the least safe assumption.

questions.question: A load projects 500 mm beyond the rear of a vehicle during daylight hours. What additional requirement applies?

options.text: A red flag measuring approximately 300 mm x 300 mm must be displayed
A white flag must be displayed
No marking is required unless the projection exceeds 1 metre
Hazard lights must be activated

questions.explanation: A load projecting more than 300 mm beyond the rear must be marked by day with a red flag of about 300 mm x 300 mm.

questions.question: A driver of a private motor vehicle notices a blue sign indicating parking for tour buses. The parking area is completely empty. What is the correct interpretation?

options.text: Any vehicle may park there if no tour buses are present
Only tour buses may use the parking area, regardless of whether it is occupied
Private vehicles may park there for up to 15 minutes
The parking area may be used by any vehicle outside business hours

questions.explanation: This blue reservation sign reserves the parking area exclusively for tour buses, even when it is empty.

questions.question: Which of the following vehicles is required by law to carry at least one double-sided emergency warning triangle?

options.text: Motorcycles
All motor vehicles registered for the first time on or after 1 July 2006 (including motor cars)
Only minibuses and heavy goods vehicles
Only emergency vehicles like ambulances

questions.explanation: Motor vehicles (including cars) first registered on or after 1 July 2006 must carry at least one emergency warning triangle.

questions.question: A driver sees a warning sign showing an aircraft. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: Aircraft have right of way over all road traffic
The road ahead leads directly onto a runway
Low-flying aircraft may distract drivers or create unexpected noise nearby
Vehicles transporting aviation fuel must stop ahead

questions.explanation: The aircraft warning sign warns of low-flying aircraft that may distract drivers or cause sudden noise.

questions.question: A goods vehicle is carrying standing passengers. What is the minimum height of the enclosure above the surface on which those passengers are standing?

options.text: 350 mm
60 mm
750 mm
900 mm

questions.explanation: When standing passengers are carried on a goods vehicle, the enclosure must extend at least 900 mm above the surface on which they stand.

questions.question: A warning sign indicates that the roadway ahead narrows from both sides. What should drivers expect?

options.text: The number of lanes automatically decreases
Reduced lateral clearance between vehicles
A compulsory stop ahead
Traffic will merge into a one-way roadway

questions.explanation: A road-narrows-from-both-sides warning means the roadway width decreases, so there is less lateral clearance between vehicles.

questions.question: A driver loads goods that project beyond the front of a light motor vehicle. What is the maximum permitted projection beyond the front end of the vehicle?

options.text: 150 mm
300 mm
450 mm
600 mm

questions.explanation: Goods may not project more than 300 mm beyond the front end of a light or heavy motor vehicle.
